title: Vanishing descends to a retract
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring (in the application $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$; $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ is included and gives abelian sheaves). For a scheme $T$ let $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant sheaf of rings $\underline\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For $q\ge0$ and $F$ in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ let $R^qh_*F\in\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] be the $q$-th higher direct image of the underlying abelian sheaf of $F$, $R^qh_*F=\mathcal H^q(Rh_*F)$ with $Rh_*:\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] computed with K-injective resolutions of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], as in $\mathrm{IA}_r$. Let $M$, $I$ be objects of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ with morphisms $\iota:I\to M$ and $\rho:M\to I$ of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ such that $\rho\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_I$ ($I$ is a direct summand, i.e. a retract, of $M$). If $R^qh_*M=0$ for every $q>0$, then $R^qh_*I=0$ for every $q>0$. (Computing $R^qh_*$ instead with the derived functors of $h_*:\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ gives the same underlying abelian sheaves, Stacks 0D6J (3); the proof below uses only that $R^qh_*$ is a functor, so it holds verbatim for that reading too.)

proof.text: *The retraction on underlying abelian sheaves.* A morphism of sheaves of $\underline\Lambda$-modules is a morphism of the underlying abelian sheaves, with the same composition and identities [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so forgetting the module structure is a functor $\operatorname{For}:\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. By [lem-weil-pbc-functor-preserves-retract] applied to $\operatorname{For}$, $\operatorname{For}(\rho)\circ\operatorname{For}(\iota)=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{For}I}$: the underlying abelian sheaf of $I$ is a retract of that of $M$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$. Thus it suffices to prove the desired vanishing for $f_*\mathcal J$")

proof.text: *$R^qh_*$ carries the retraction to a retraction.* Fix $q>0$. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $R^qh_*:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ is the composite of the functor sending a sheaf to the complex concentrated in degree $0$ in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the functor $Rh_*:\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ and the cohomology-sheaf functor $\mathcal H^q$; so it is a functor. By [lem-weil-pbc-functor-preserves-retract] applied to $R^qh_*$ and the retraction of step 1, $R^qh_*(\rho)\circ R^qh_*(\iota)=\mathrm{id}_{R^qh_*I}$: $R^qh_*I$ is a retract of $R^qh_*M$ in $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$. (Only functoriality is used; additivity of $R^qh_*$ is not needed.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$. Thus it suffices to prove the desired vanishing for $f_*\mathcal J$")

proof.text: *A retract of zero is zero.* $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ is an abelian category [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], in particular it has zero morphisms, and $R^qh_*M$ is a zero object by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-retract-of-zero-object] applied to the retraction of step 2, $R^qh_*I$ is a zero object: $R^qh_*I=0$. As $q>0$ was arbitrary, this is the claim.
